The competing obligation being assessed is Dana’s “imperfect duty to rescue” toward ten workers. For “pulls the lever”, the agent proposes the maxim “Pull lever to divert tram”. This is an interpretation of possible practical reasoning, not an established intention. Its purpose is Save ten; its chosen means are Tram strikes side-track worker. The proposed justification is: Cannot will rule that permits killing innocents as side-effect rescue. The agent assesses the maxim as indefensible, and the action as impermissible. For Dana’s option “pulls the lever”, the ledger records conflicted. The agent’s stated reason is: Intervention causes death of protected party.. The agent assesses Dana’s duty “do not kill an innocent person” toward all workers. Dana is the duty-bearer; all workers is the protected party. The competing obligation being assessed is Dana’s “imperfect duty to rescue” toward ten workers. For “does not pull the lever”, the agent proposes the maxim “Refrain from diverting tram”. This is an interpretation of possible practical reasoning, not an established intention. Its purpose is Avoid killing; its chosen means are Take no action affecting tram path. The proposed justification is: Can will omission when proposed action is killing. The agent assesses the maxim as defensible, and the action as permissible. For Dana’s option “does not pull the lever”, the ledger records permissible. The agent’s stated reason is: No act that kills; harm permitted is not agent-caused. The ledger retains unresolved issues; this does not establish that one duty overrides the other.
